call_points.text: Of the ₹240 Cr dredging order book, ₹200 Cr is expected to be executed this year.
Shipbuilding to scale significantly from Q4FY27 as the yard commissions.
Subcontracting charges to stay at 5-6% of turnover from FY26, mostly shipbuilding work routed to the yard.
Shipbuilding margins are 15-20% pre-subsidy but can exceed 35% post-subsidy on delivery.
Shipbuilding working capital is covered by stage payments; no new loans needed for execution.
Asked for Green Tug IRR, management gave a 75% EBITDA margin and 15-year contracts instead, directing the analyst to IR.
Two dredgers adding 12,000 cubic meters of hopper capacity can be bought in under 90 days.
Bid pipeline of over ₹2,000 Cr, all domestic, expected to convert over the next three months.
Bid pipeline split: dredging about ₹950 Cr, shipbuilding about ₹400 Cr, green tugs about ₹600 Cr.
Shipbuilding EBITDA margin is 25-30% before subsidy and 35-40% including the 10-15% government subsidy.
Cash including fixed deposits is over ₹350 Cr, with free cash of about ₹300 Cr.
Tonnage tax applies only to vessel operations, not shipbuilding; tax will not exceed 0.1% of chartering or dredging revenue.
Bahrain and Myanmar operations are paused; vessels moved to India, and Bahrain will restart only when the situation normalises.
Shipbuilding subsidiary is 51% owned now, to be raised to 75%.

operating_notes.text: Shipyard site at Saphale, Palghar has ~188m waterfront access and a natural slipway with ~6m high-tide draft on the Vaitarna River, near the upcoming Vadhvan Port.
Phased plan: Phase I workboats and tugs, Phase II repair facilities and floating dry docks, Phase III large-scale vessels.
Of the ₹284.81 Cr preferential issue, ₹260.07 Cr was held in fixed deposits with Bandhan Bank, Yes Bank and HDFC Bank at 6.22–7.20% as at March 31, 2026.
₹11.11 Cr of the preferential issue amount was yet to be received as at March 31, 2026.
Company opted for the Tonnage Tax Scheme under Chapter XII-G of the Income-tax Act, 1961 for qualifying shipping activities.
FY26 order wins were ₹1,075 Cr, the highest in KMEW's history, and the order book was about ₹1,400 Cr at FY26-end.
Bid pipeline of over ₹2,000 Cr, all domestic, split into dredging about ₹950 Cr, shipbuilding about ₹400 Cr and green tugs about ₹600 Cr.
Shipbuilding EBITDA margin is 25-30% before subsidy and 35-40% including the 10-15% government subsidy.
Q1FY27 revenue mix: dredging about 80%, shipbuilding 9%, chartering 3-5%.
Order book over ₹1,300 Cr across 8 dredging, 15 charter and hire and 4 shipbuilding contracts, excluding ₹200 Cr intercompany orders placed with Knowledge Shipyard.
Bid pipeline ₹3,500+ Cr; historical hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years.
Received requests from 16 promoter group members for re-classification to the public category.

timeline.summary: KMEW said its subsidiary Knowledge Shipyard acquired ~15 acres of waterfront land at Saphale, Palghar, with a 5-acre option, for a phased shipyard near the upcoming Vadhvan Port; no cost or timeline was disclosed.
2026-05-15: CARE Ratings' monitoring report showed ₹13.63 Cr of KMEW's ₹284.81 Cr preferential issue utilised by March 31, 2026, with ₹260.07 Cr unutilised and nil deviation from objects.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹67.62 Cr (+42.4% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹26.21 Cr.
On June 2, 2026, Knowledge Marine disclosed open market share purchases totaling 5,326 equity shares by its Managing Director, CEO, and CTO.
Knowledge Marine disclosed open market share purchases of 1,545 equity shares by designated persons Sujay and Dinesh Kewalramani.
AJAY KOTWAL (AVDHOOT Digitally signed) disclosed the Q4FY26 earnings call audio recording on June 5, 2026, available at https://www.kmew.in/investor-information.html.
2026-06-12: KMEW's FY26 earnings call transcript guided 30% revenue growth for FY27-28, 35-40% EBITDA margin, and ₹400-500 Cr FY27 capex, with a ₹1,400 Cr order book and ₹2,000 Cr bid pipeline.

2026-09-02: KMEW's Q1FY27 earnings call transcript showed revenue of ₹115.41 Cr (+138% YoY), EBITDA margin of ~64%, PAT of ₹62.75 Cr, an order book over ₹1,300 Cr and FY27 growth guidance raised to north of 60%.
Knowledge Marine received requests from 16 promoter group members on October 19, 2026, to reclassify from the promoter group to the public category.
